title: WASSCE Geography: Complete Preparation
description: A full 10-module WASSCE Geography preparation course aligned to the WAEC syllabus: map reading & practical geography, physical geography, climate & vegetation, human & economic geography, environmental geography, regional geography (Liberia & West Africa), fieldwork skills, revision, and a full mock examination with a Certificate of Completion.
outcomes: Understand the WAEC Geography exam structure and marking scheme
Read and interpret maps: scale, distance, bearings, grid references and contours
Explain physical geography: rocks, weathering, rivers, volcanoes and landforms
Understand climate, vegetation and human/economic geography
Analyse environmental issues and the regional geography of Liberia and West Africa
Carry out fieldwork skills and apply exam techniques with mock practice
about: This is the complete TIH WASSCE Geography preparation course, organised into ten modules aligned to the WAEC Geography syllabus and examination structure (objective, theory and practical/map-reading).

Every content lesson has a video and printable notes with diagrams and maps; downloadable resources include a map-reading guide, physical- and regional-geography guides and fieldwork guides. The course ends with a full mock examination and a Certificate of Completion.
Use this course together with the official WAEC syllabus, an atlas, your teacher’s guidance and WAEC past questions for best results.
requirements: A phone or computer with internet
A ruler, protractor and pencil for map work
An atlas (or Google Maps/Earth) for regional study
A geography notebook for diagrams and revision

lessons.title: 2.1 Types of Maps
lessons.html:
WASSCE Geography · Module 2: Map Reading & Practical GeographyWAEC syllabus aligned

Types of Maps

This lesson builds map reading & practical geography through clear definitions, diagrams/maps and timed practice. Watch the video, study the notes, diagrams and maps, then complete the two exercises before the short quiz.

Key points

  • Define Types of Maps precisely and know how WAEC tests it in objective, theory and practical (map) papers.
  • Study a labelled diagram/map and the points examiners reward.
  • Practise with past-question-style items, using sketches, maps and real West African examples.

📥 Guide: Map Reading Essentials

  • Scale: e.g. 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map = 50,000 cm (0.5 km) on the ground.
  • Distance: measure with a ruler/string, then convert using the scale.
  • Direction: compass points; bearings measured clockwise from North (000°–360°).
  • Grid references: read EASTINGS first, then NORTHINGS ("along the corridor, up the stairs").
  • Contours: lines joining points of equal height; close contours = steep slope.

Downloadable: Print → Save as PDF to keep this guide in your revision folder.

Exercises

The Earth and the Solar System

This lesson builds physical geography through clear definitions, diagrams/maps and timed practice. Watch the video, study the notes, diagrams and maps, then complete the two exercises before the short quiz.

📥 Guide: Physical Geography

  • Rock types: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.
  • Weathering: physical, chemical and biological breakdown of rock in place.
  • Erosion wears away and transports material; deposition lays it down.
  • Rivers: source → upper/middle/lower course → mouth; features include V-valleys, meanders, deltas.
  • Vulcanicity: earthquakes and volcanoes occur mainly at plate boundaries.

WASSCE Geography · Module 6: Environmental GeographyWAEC syllabus aligned

Disaster Management

This lesson builds environmental geography through understanding the concept and applying it to WAEC-style questions and map work. Watch the video, study the notes, diagrams and maps, then complete the two exercises before the short quiz.

Key points

  • Define Disaster Management precisely and know how WAEC tests it in objective, theory and practical (map) papers.
  • Study a labelled diagram/map and the points examiners reward.
  • Practise with past-question-style items, using sketches, maps and real West African examples.

📥 Guide: Environmental Geography

  • Deforestation: clearing forests → erosion, loss of biodiversity, climate impact.
  • Desertification: productive land turning to desert (drought + poor land use).
  • Soil conservation: terracing, contour ploughing, afforestation, crop rotation.
  • Sustainable development: meeting present needs without harming the future.
  • Disaster management: preparedness, response and recovery.

📥 Guide: Map Reading Essentials

  • Scale: e.g. 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map = 50,000 cm (0.5 km) on the ground.
  • Distance: measure with a ruler/string, then convert using the scale.
  • Direction: compass points; bearings measured clockwise from North (000°–360°).
  • Grid references: read EASTINGS first, then NORTHINGS ("along the corridor, up the stairs").
  • Contours: lines joining points of equal height; close contours = steep slope.
